questions.question: What is the primary difference between Console.WriteLine() and Console.Write() in C#?
options: Console.WriteLine() appends a newline at the end of the printed text, while Console.Write() does not
Console.WriteLine() only works with strings, while Console.Write() works with integers
Console.Write() flushes the buffer, while Console.WriteLine() stores text in memory only
There is no difference; they are aliases for the same method
questions.explanation: Console.WriteLine() outputs the text followed immediately by the current line terminator, moving the cursor to the next line. Console.Write() outputs text without a trailing newline.

questions.question: Which namespace contains the Console class in the .NET runtime?
questions.explanation: The Console class is a static class in the root System namespace (System.Console).

questions.question: What is the output of the expression 15 / 4 in C#?
questions.explanation: Because both 15 and 4 are integer literals, C# performs integer division and truncates the fractional portion, resulting in 3.

questions.question: What is the result of the modulo operation 17 % 5 in C#?
questions.explanation: 17 divided by 5 equals 3 with a remainder of 2 (5 * 3 + 2 = 17).

questions.question: In C#, what does the escape sequence '\n' represent in a string literal?
questions.explanation: The escape sequence \n represents the linefeed / newline character.

questions.question: What is the evaluated output of the expression: 4 + 2 * 3 in C#?
questions.explanation: Multiplication (*) has higher precedence than addition (+), so 2 * 3 evaluates first to 6, followed by 4 + 6 = 10.

questions.question: How do you write a single-line comment in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, single-line comments begin with // and extend to the end of the line.

questions.question: What is the canonical entry point signature for a traditional C# console application?
questions.explanation: The standard entry point method recognized by the C# compiler is static void Main(string[] args) or static int Main(string[] args).

questions.question: What character must terminate every statement in C#?
questions.explanation: C# requires each statement to be terminated with a semicolon (;).

questions.question: What will Console.WriteLine("Result: " + 5 + 5); print to the console?
options: Result: 55 (string concatenation from left to right)
questions.explanation: Evaluation proceeds left to right: "Result: " + 5 yields "Result: 5", and "Result: 5" + 5 yields "Result: 55".
